chapter: Russell and Armstrong years, Goodman and the road
title: Benny Goodman and Harry James copying at the Saratoga Club
summary: He says Goodman and Harry James copied the Russell band's solos on paper at the Saratoga Club.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: What was your impression of people like Paul Whiteman and Benny Goodman?
Bill Davis?
No, Paul Whiteman, and Benny Goodman.
I think he's very nice.
... Yeah, I met him. I remember meeting him a couple of times. That was when we were playing across from him at Roseland. We had Bill Polk (?).
Do you remember what year that was?
Got too much
What did you think of Benny Goodman?
when he got through stealing. He'd steal

I think Benny's OK. ... every night, he and Harry James at the Saratoga Club. Soon as they get through, they wouldn't even change clothes, bring a pencil and paper and sit down and write ... but they can play now.
Sit down and write what, other people's solos?
They used to copy em like that.
He'd copy them, yeah. Too bad they didn't have tape recorders in those days. No, they had pencil and paper and write.
He'd just remember everything, huh?
Yeah.
Who was he stealing from, everybody?
Anybody he could out of the band and that was the favorite band then.
Always the black musicians though?
Always, yeah.
And you said Harry James too?
Harry James sure did. He used to listen to the same band, the Louis Russell band (...) Benny Goodman in 1929, Benny Goodman didn't play no jazz.
What was he doing then?
Stealing. Learning how to play.
Where did you first meet him?
I met him at the Saratoga Club.
What was he doing?
Came in there stealing.
I mean, was he from New York or did he just hang around New York?
No, he was working in New York. Oh, I don't know, he was working in some place hotel downtown. They get off early and come up.
